--- ## Walkthrough The AWS `providerSpec.availabilityZone` VAP enforcement test is updated to dynamically mutate the availability zone field by appending `"-changed"` to its current value, replacing the previous hard-coded constant while maintaining the VAP blocking validation expectation. ## Changes |Cohort / File(s)|Summary| |---|---| |**Test Mutation Update**
`e2e/machine_migration_vap_tests.go`|Modified test to dynamically append `"-changed"` to the current availability zone value instead of using a hard-coded `testAvailabilityZone` constant; VAP blocking behavior remains unchanged.| ## Estimated code review effort 🎯 1 (Trivial) | ⏱️ ~3 minutes --- > [!IMPORTANT] > ## Pre-merge checks failed > > Please resolve all errors before merging. Addressing warnings is optional. ### ❌ Failed checks (1 warning, 1 inconclusive) | Check name | Status | Explanation | Resolution | | :---------------------------------: | :------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Microshift Test Compatibility | ⚠️ Warning | Test modifies Machine API providerSpec.Placement.AvailabilityZone, which is unavailable on MicroShift clusters. | Add [apigroup:machine.openshift.io] tag to skip test on MicroShift or wrap with exutil.IsMicroShiftCluster() check. | | Stable And Deterministic Test Names | ❓ Inconclusive | The test file e2e/machine_migration_vap_tests.go could not be located or accessed in the repository to verify Ginkgo test name stability. | Verify the correct repository branch is loaded and the test file exists and is accessible before re-running the assessment. |
✅ Passed checks (10 passed) | Check name | Status | Explanation | | :----------------------------------------------: | :------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Description Check | ✅ Passed | Check skipped - CodeRabbit’s high-level summary is enabled. | | Title check | ✅ Passed | The title directly addresses the main change: fixing an e2e test flake by removing hard-coded availability zone dependency that fails when workers are in specific zones. | | Docstring Coverage | ✅ Passed | No functions found in the changed files to evaluate docstring coverage. Skipping docstring coverage check. | | Linked Issues check | ✅ Passed | Check skipped because no linked issues were found for this pull request. | | Out of Scope Changes check | ✅ Passed | Check skipped because no linked issues were found for this pull request. | | Test Structure And Quality | ✅ Passed | The e2e test file demonstrates strong adherence to all five quality requirements: single responsibility with 17 focused test blocks, proper setup/cleanup using BeforeAll/DeferCleanup patterns, appropriate timeouts on all Eventually calls, meaningful assertion messages, and consistency with established codebase patterns. | | Single Node Openshift (Sno) Test Compatibility | ✅ Passed | The PR modifies an existing test rather than adding a new Ginkgo e2e test, so the SNO compatibility check does not apply. | | Topology-Aware Scheduling Compatibility | ✅ Passed | PR modifies only e2e test file, not deployment manifests, operator code, or controllers, making it out of scope for custom check requirements. | | Ote Binary Stdout Contract | ✅ Passed | File contains only Ginkgo test code with no process-level functions that could write to stdout. All output uses GinkgoWriter correctly. PR change modifies test logic without introducing stdout writes. | | Ipv6 And Disconnected Network Test Compatibility | ✅ Passed | Test file contains no IPv4-specific assumptions or external connectivity requirements. It operates entirely within the cluster using Kubernetes API calls to validate VAP enforcement rules on machine resources. |
